topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the lecture series, and sets the learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology.

topics.label: Biological Foundations of Cancer and Sources of Mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and outline the endogenous, inherited, and environmental origins of mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the relationship between environmental carcinogens and cancer incidence through public health observations and geographic epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious pathogens contribute to malignant transformation, highlighting the multi-factorial etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical pathways through which physical radiation and metabolized chemical agents induce direct DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic factors in carcinogenesis, including tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarizing key themes in carcinogenicity and discussing everyday risk-benefit decisions regarding exposures.
